body: Cross linking #91453 because I'm pretty sure that's the same underlying issue

Fields of type `aggregate_metric_double` are summary fields that only support a limited set of aggregations. 

Supported aggregations `min`, `max`, `sum`, `value_count` and `avg`. 

The `default_metric` subfield is used for delegating queries, but not aggregations. 

Other aggs such as `cardinality`, `percentile` or `terms` are not supported at the moment. You can find more information in the [field type documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/aggregate-metric-double.html#aggregate-metric-double-uses)

@csoulios Thx for replying. The documentation is clearly misleading then, see the screenshot. To be honest, I wouldn't even have given the field a try if it was clear we can't run percentiles aggs in it...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5468291/212400795-21c05f95-76a6-4503-82c2-eead57ce6d98.png)

Cheers,
David

@ddolcimascolo you are right that the documentation is wrong there and I will make sure we fix the misleading part. Thank you for reporting this. 

FWIW `percentiles` aggregation (and more) are supported by the [`histogram` field type](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/histogram.html). Maybe this can work for you.

Yeah, I've noticed the `histogram` field. Will definitely take a deeper look, thx for the sggestion

David
